opening: This second act adds a subnet to network. Its id is known only after apply.

pull-request.prompt: Add a second subnet to network; put a worker in it.
pull-request.reply: Opened pull request {pull}. network adds subnet b, app adds a worker in it, edge allows its range. Next: plan all three.

pull-request.status: Planning network, app and edge together

tips.title: One plan, three roots
tips.body: With terraform.compose on, chant writes one root that calls network, app and edge as modules and plans it once. It posts one note with one digest.

planned.reply: One plan across 3 roots. Only one value is unknown: subnet b's id, which app's worker needs.

planned.prompt: What depends on the new subnet?
planned.reply: {dependents} resources: app's worker and edge's allowlist.

tips.title: Known after apply
tips.body: AWS gives a new subnet its id only when it creates it. In the composed plan app's subnet_id and edge's parameter read network's output, so the plan marks them known after apply instead of planning on a stand-in.

approved.status: Recording your approval on the pull request

tips.title: One approval
tips.body: The approval binds the one plan, unknown id included. The apply needs no second plan of app or edge: the id reaches them inside the same apply.

merged.status: Merging and applying network, app and edge in one pass

tips.title: Variables, not remote state
tips.body: Each root reads the one before it through variables that chant fills from its outputs with stackOutput. In the composed run those become module outputs, so a new value reaches its readers inside the one apply.

applying.status: Applying network, app and edge together

tips.title: Each root keeps its own state
tips.body: The composed apply works on a merged copy of the three states and writes each root's part back to its own state when it ends.

tips.title: A stock chant project
tips.body: These are three Terraform roots in a chant project. The pull request pipeline is the one chant generates for the project. No other tool is in it.

applied.reply: Done. Subnet b was created and app's worker got its id in the same apply.
No. chant took each root's state lock for the apply and let go of all three when the states were written back.

tips.title: Locking
tips.body: chant holds each root's state lock from the plan it applies until that root's state is written back. A state it could not write is kept, and its lock stays held until a later run writes it.
